title: Crackle paste texture on air-dry clay
subtitle: Creating an aged crackle surface on an air-dry piece using acrylic crackle medium
excerpt: Crackle paste medium, when applied over a base coat and allowed to dry, forms a network of fine cracks in the top colour that reveal the base colour beneath. Applied to air-dry clay, the technique gives a deliberately aged or fractured ceramic look. No kiln required: the crackle is entirely in the paint layer.
sourceNotes: Crackle medium technique derived from decorative paint practice adapted for air-dry clay surfaces. No kiln; the crackle effect is achieved with acrylic medium, not glaze.

glossaryTerms.definition: Air-dried but unfired clay. The surface must be bone-dry before applying paint or crackle medium.

content.text: Crackle medium shrinks at a different rate from the base coat below it. As it dries, it pulls. The top colour cracks into patches. The base colour shows through the gaps. A thin coat gives fine hairline cracks. A thick coat gives larger fractures. On air-dry clay, the result looks like an aged ceramic surface.

air-dry clay piece, already sealed with one coat of acrylic gesso or primer. Acrylic crackle medium (available from art supply shops). Two contrasting acrylic paint colours: the base colour will show through the cracks, and the top colour will carry the crackle. A wide soft brush for applying medium and paint. A sealant coat to finish.
Apply one coat of the base acrylic paint colour to the sealed clay piece. Allow to dry fully: 30 minutes to an hour.

Apply the crackle medium over the dry base coat. Apply thickly for large cracks, thinly for fine crackle. Do not over-brush: apply in a single pass of the brush per area and leave it. Brush marks in the crackle medium become the direction of the cracks.
Allow the crackle medium to dry completely: this is critical. The medium should be pale and translucent when dry, not milky-white. This takes 30 to 60 minutes depending on thickness.

Apply the top coat acrylic paint colour over the dry crackle medium in a single, deliberate stroke per area. Do not go back over areas you have already painted: re-painting disrupts the cracking action. The cracks will begin to form as the paint dries, over 10 to 20 minutes.
Allow the top coat to dry without touching or moving the piece. Any disturbance during drying tears the crackle unpredictably.
When fully dry, apply two coats of acrylic sealant over the crackled surface to protect the paint and prevent the cracks from attracting dust.
What it looks like when right

A successful crackle has an irregular network of cracks distributed across the surface, with the base colour visible in the crack lines. The cracks should be sharp-edged rather than fuzzy. The overall effect reads as an aged, antiqued surface.
No cracks forming: the crackle medium was not dry enough when the top coat was applied. Wait the full drying time.

Top coat peeling rather than cracking: the top paint coat was applied too thick, or the brand of crackle medium is not compatible with the top paint. Test on a clay offcut before applying to the final piece.
Only small patches cracking: the crackle medium was applied in patches rather than uniformly. Apply in one even coat.

rows.problem: Cracks all running in the same direction
rows.cause: Single-direction brush strokes in the crackle medium
rows.fix: Apply crackle medium with cross-direction strokes for a more random crack pattern.

rows.problem: Base colour shows through in larger blotches, not cracks
rows.cause: Top coat too thin, or crackle medium applied too thick
rows.fix: Adjust: thinner crackle medium and a thicker top paint coat. Test on scrap clay before the main piece.
